title: Understanding IR singularities in the Loop-Tree Duality
authors: Germán Rodrigo, Leandro Cieri, Prasanna K. Dhani, Roger J. Hernández-Pinto, Jorge J. Martínez de Lejarza, Salvador A. Ochoa-Oregon, Konstantinos Pyretzidis, Selomit Ramírez-Uribe, David F. Rentería-Estrada, Andrés E. Rentería-Olivo, José Ríos-Sánchez, German F. R. Sborlini, Surabhi Tiwari, Juan P. Uribe-Ramírez
abstract: One of the main advantages of the Loop-Tree Duality representation of scattering amplitudes is that it makes the origin of infrared and threshold singularities particularly transparent. This talk reviews recent progress in describing how singularities emerge and cancel at the level of scattering and vacuum amplitudes, discusses a novel strategy to efficiently construct finite integrals, and presents a complementary perspective based on encoding the underlying causal and singular structure in terms of qubits and quantum circuits.
summary: This work details how Loop-Tree Duality simplifies the understanding of infrared and threshold singularities in complex quantum field theory calculations. It introduces a novel approach to construct finite scattering amplitudes by enforcing causal constraints. Furthermore, it provides a unique perspective by encoding this underlying causal structure using qubits and quantum circuits.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex theoretical challenge of understanding and constructing finite, infrared (IR) and threshold-free multiloop Feynman integrals in Quantum Field Theory.
main_result: The Loop-Tree Duality (LTD) provides a transparent framework for identifying these finite integrals, and the methodology can be mapped onto a quantum circuit structure using qubits.
method: The authors review LTD, which reformulates loop integrations to explicitly handle singularities, and propose encoding the causal structure of the amplitudes using qubits and quantum circuits.
model_or_system: The physical system is Quantum Field Theory (QFT) calculations involving multiloop scattering amplitudes. The mathematical framework utilizes Loop-Tree Duality (LTD) and is conceptually mapped onto quantum circuits.
key_observables: Infrared (IR) and threshold singularities, and the construction of finite, threshold-free scattering amplitudes.
important_parameters: Loop integration parameters, external and internal momenta, and the structure of causal propagators.
main_assumptions: The LTD representation is assumed to inherently enforce causality by restricting configurations to acyclic paths, which is key to avoiding spurious singularities.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate causal propagators, examples of collinear configurations leading to physical thresholds, and the directed states of a one-loop three-point function distinguishing finite from singular configurations.
paper_structure: The paper reviews the LTD advantage in visualizing singularities, details novel strategies for constructing finite integrals (including pole vanishing conditions), and concludes by presenting a complementary perspective using qubits and quantum circuits to encode the causal structure.
why_interesting: While the core physics is QFT, the explicit mapping of the causal/singular structure onto qubits and quantum circuits provides a direct, novel application of quantum information concepts to high-energy theoretical physics calculations.
